Versions verified in the repository include Java 21 and Spring Boot 3.5.6. PostgreSQL is configured through environment variables.
The clients stay thin: visibility, eligibility and authorization are enforced by the backend.
Architecture reflects the actual repository structure: Flutter and Angular clients call the Spring Boot API, which persists to PostgreSQL.
Modules are derived from controllers, services, entity mappings and the two frontend clients.

Actual table names include users, departments, students, companies, placement_drives, placement_applications, placement_drive_rounds and placement_round_results. The diagram emphasizes the placement relationships rather than every column.
Student uses enrollment number. Staff uses university email.
BCrypt checks the stored password. Disabled or unsupported accounts fail closed.

Protected services reload the account and use current role/active state.
/api/me returns safe identity, role, active status and department data when present. Staff accounts do not require a Student row.
This reflects the implemented compatibility path: student enrollment login is preserved while staff login uses identifier/email and does not require a student profile.
